sources.reviewed_locator: Field Reference, Pipeline Stages, and Stability
sources.decision: Pipeline entries report material request or response effects, stage kinds may grow, and unknown stages are opaque. This supports rejecting every nonempty pipeline while decoding unrelated additive metadata permissively.

sources.reviewed_locator: Default Plugin Settings and Plugin precedence
sources.decision: Request controls may be affected by account or organization plugin policy; metadata must therefore remain an observed processing-integrity gate.
Context compression changes prompt content and is a material effect under the current Neuvetra policy.

primary_evidence_decision.m32_boundary: M32 retained only the failed field name and not the pipeline value. It supplies no positive fixture and no evidence for a benign nonempty form.
primary_evidence_decision.accepted_contract: Only an absent pipeline or an empty array may pass. A non-array is shape; every nonempty array is material_effect. No new provider behavior is admitted.

independent_inline_probe.method: Bun inline imports with synthetic in-memory response objects, injected fetch, in-memory stage events and accounting; no application file added
covered: Absent and empty pipelines pass for all three stages.
Null, scalar, string and object values return shape and fail validation.
Malformed, nested, sparse, plugin-like, unknown and very large nonempty arrays return material_effect and fail validation with constant-time length inspection.
Pipeline-only failures emit router_pipeline and a finite label without router_identity_field or accepted openrouter identity metadata.
A sensitive nested marker is absent from terminal events.
Valid native HTTP-200 cost settles once despite rejection; missing cost becomes uncertain without a metadata lookup; settlement failure preserves router_pipeline and adds uncertainty.
A simultaneous response-model conflict remains an identity failure while the independent pipeline predicate remains material_effect.
independent_inline_probe.initial_probe_correction: The first probe attempt incorrectly used a JavaScript default parameter for the intended missing-cost case, restoring the cost and causing the QA expectation to fail. The corrected hasCost switch produced the reported 148-pass result; this was a probe defect, not an application defect.

profile_binding.result: The semantic answering policy is unchanged and the OpenRouter transport/diagnostic profile changes intentionally. M32 run artifacts cannot be reused.

findings.identity_separation: Pipeline processing is no longer mislabeled as provider identity. Strict requested, response and selected model/provider, strategy, attempt, BYOK, cache, endpoint and optional-attempt identity checks remain in force.
findings.fail_closed_processing: The implementation accepts only absence or an empty array. It does not inspect, retain, normalize or approve any nonempty stage and cannot silently accept a future stage kind.
findings.diagnostic_safety: Only router_pipeline plus shape or material_effect is retained. Raw pipeline values and nested data do not enter the stage event.
findings.accounting_separation: Valid same-response cost can settle the one rejected POST without creating accepted identity or an answer. Missing or invalid cost remains uncertain, settlement failure cannot authorize later work, and no failure-path generation lookup or provider retry was added.
findings.additive_metadata: Unrelated additive router metadata remains ignored rather than becoming an approval or a failure, consistent with the documented stability boundary.

limitations: This PASS covers only the pinned offline M33 implementation, tests and milestone record. It does not establish the value or cause observed in M32.
Synthetic responses do not establish that current account and request controls will produce an absent or empty live pipeline.
No live provider verification, answer correctness, browser mechanics, invoice finality, deployment or release acceptance is demonstrated.

A later paid check requires a newly frozen profile and run package, current primary-source recheck, bounded cost/stage/no-retry rules, mechanical capture plan, independent preflight and separate board authorization. M32 must not be replayed.
verdict: PASS for the M33 offline provider-pipeline integrity repair; not live or release acceptance.
